correctness.rationale: Direct proof: block upper triangular structure matrix has determinant 1/2. The first two idempotent equations have exactly (0,0),(1,1) over each field of characteristic !=2. Subsequent equations have forcing state h=0 or 1/4, with root choices {0,1} before the first nonzero step and unique 1/2 thereafter, giving exactly n explicitly listed points. The standalone standard-library checker tests rational formulas in dimensions 2..12 and all field vectors for p=3,5,7 in dimensions 2..5 (23860 vectors). All checks passed; unbounded validity is proved symbolically.

originality.rationale: The exact point count n in every dimension n>=3 over fields of characteristic !=2 is not stated in the inspected 2026 survey, which reports only complex triangular constructions with at least n+1 idempotents and poses the full spectrum as Conjecture 6. The idempotent-existence theorem and full-support classification do not imply the uniform exact count. Dedicated research-index searches and web searches for the count and its discriminant-collision formulation found no matching result. This is qualified originality rather than a proof of world-first priority.
residual_risks: The full historic literature on isolated quadratic fixed-point schemes and 3-dimensional evolution algebra classification was not exhaustively inspected; an implicit equivalent may exist.
The survey describes a broader open conjecture and evidence, but passing a literature search cannot establish absolute novelty.
No independent mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The 2026 survey explicitly asks for all possible counts of idempotents of perfect n-dimensional complex evolution algebras and notes that its triangular complex constructions only give at least n+1 points. The uniform exact n-point construction fills a natural missing value for every n>=3, rather than a random special case. The same explicit matrices work in every field of characteristic different from two, and the double-root propagation mechanism explains the point-count drop. It does not settle the unresolved possibility of exactly two points for n>=3.
